# Setup

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| cache: true
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import umap
import hdbscan
import seaborn as sns
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA

# 1. Load data
res_df = pd.read_csv("C:/Users/mcmur/OneDrive/Documents/GitHub/Math-4810_Capstone/data/MLS_Land_Sales.csv").select_dtypes(include=['number'])
puma_df = pd.read_csv("C:/Users/mcmur/OneDrive/Documents/GitHub/Math-4810_Capstone/data/PUMA2.csv").select_dtypes(include=['number'])

# 2. Separate data - FIXED puma_target reference
res_target = res_df['Sold Price'] 
puma_target = puma_df['Sold Price'] 

# 3. Drop target-leakage columns
res_features = res_df.drop(columns=['Sold Price', 'List Price', 'Original List Price'])
puma_features = puma_df.drop(columns=['Sold Price', 'Adjusted SP'])

def get_scaled_data(df):
    X = df.fillna(0)
    X = X.loc[:, X.var() > 1e-4]
    return StandardScaler().fit_transform(X)

def plot_scree(scaled_data, title):
    pca = PCA().fit(scaled_data)
    cum_var = np.cumsum(pca.explained_variance_ratio_)
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 4))
    plt.plot(range(1, len(cum_var) + 1), cum_var, marker='o', color='magenta')
    plt.axhline(y=0.9, color='white', linestyle='--', label='90% Variance')
    plt.title(f"{title} - Cumulative Explained Variance")
    plt.ylabel("Cumulative Variance")
    plt.legend()
    plt.show()

import matplotlib.colors as colors

def plot_umap(scaled_data, target, nn, md, title):
    pca_data = PCA(n_components=0.9).fit_transform(scaled_data)
    reducer = umap.UMAP(n_neighbors=nn, min_dist=md, random_state=42)
    embedding = reducer.fit_transform(pca_data)
    
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
    
    # We use LogNorm to stretch the color distribution
    # We use target.clip(lower=1) to avoid log(0) errors
    scatter = plt.scatter(embedding[:,0], embedding[:,1], 
                         c=target, 
                         norm=colors.LogNorm(vmin=target.min()+1, vmax=target.max()),
                         cmap='viridis', s=10, alpha=0.6)
    
    plt.title(f"{title} Projection (Log-Scaled Colors)")
    plt.colorbar(scatter, label="Sold Price ($)")
    plt.show()

def plot_price_correlation(df_features, target_series, title):
    # Only look at the columns that actually have data variation
    kept_columns = df_features.columns[df_features.fillna(0).var() > 1e-4]
    temp_df = df_features[kept_columns].copy()
    temp_df['Sold Price'] = target_series
    
    corrs = temp_df.corr()['Sold Price'].sort_values(ascending=False).drop('Sold Price').head(10)
    
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
    corrs.plot.bar(color='gold')
    plt.title(f"Top Features Driving Sold Price: {title}")
    plt.show()

def plot_feature_importance(df_features, scaled_data, title):
    """Shows which variables define the PCA space, matching cleaned column counts."""
    # 1. Identify which columns were actually kept (non-zero variance)
    # This ensures the index (32) matches the values (25)
    kept_columns = df_features.columns[df_features.fillna(0).var() > 1e-4]
    
    # 2. Run PCA
    pca = PCA(n_components=0.9).fit(scaled_data)
    loadings = np.abs(pca.components_)
    
    # 3. Create Series with the correct matching length
    pca_importance = pd.Series(
        loadings.sum(axis=0), 
        index=kept_columns
    ).sort_values(ascending=False).head(10)

    # 4. Plot
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
    pca_importance.plot.bar(color='skyblue')
    plt.title(f"Top 10 Features Defining the Data Structure: {title}")
    plt.ylabel("Sum of Absolute PCA Loadings")
    plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
    plt.show()

def plot_umap_natural(scaled_data, nn, md, title):
    pca_data = PCA(n_components=0.9).fit_transform(scaled_data)
    reducer = umap.UMAP(n_neighbors=nn, min_dist=md, random_state=42)
    embedding = reducer.fit_transform(pca_data)
    
    clusterer = hdbscan.HDBSCAN(min_cluster_size=100)
    labels = clusterer.fit_predict(embedding)
    
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
    plt.scatter(embedding[:,0], embedding[:,1], c=labels, cmap='Spectral', s=10, alpha=0.8)
    plt.title(f"{title} - Natural Clusters")
    plt.colorbar(label="Cluster ID")
    plt.show()
    
    return labels

def get_detailed_summary(df_original, cluster_labels, title):
    """
    Creates a summary table for clusters using the most important features.
    """
    # 1. Attach labels to the original data
    temp_df = df_original.copy()
    temp_df['Cluster'] = cluster_labels
    
    # 2. Identify the top features based on correlation to Sold Price
    # This ensures we aren't looking at "boring" constant columns
    corrs = temp_df.corr()['Sold Price'].abs().sort_values(ascending=False)
    # Get the top 8 features (excluding Sold Price itself)
    top_features = corrs.index[1:9].tolist()
    
    # 3. Group and calculate means
    cols_to_summarize = ['Sold Price'] + top_features
    summary = temp_df[temp_df['Cluster'] != -1].groupby('Cluster')[cols_to_summarize].mean()
    
    return summary.round(2)

# Prepare scaled data
res_scaled = get_scaled_data(res_features)
puma_scaled = get_scaled_data(puma_features)
```

## Kept Columns 

I am only keeping numeric columns. I have also dropped the following for being too noisy:

- 'List Price'
- 'Original List Price'
- 'Adjusted SP'
